release_state: FOR REVIEW - HOLD NO EXTERNAL RELEASE

supersedes.note: The prior receipt was accurate when written: no build existed anywhere in scope. It remains byte-identical at its published hash. This record supersedes by addition.

build.dependency_note: Standard library only. Runs on the authorized Windows workstation with nothing but Python installed.

audit_exit_code_ruling: Exit 2 is the correct result on this host. A Linux lane cannot see C:\DataBoss, so every Windows-local item is UNREACHABLE and V12 is not called verified. The tower refuses to report a clean result it did not earn.
properties_enforced_and_tested: only the canonical 01_QUEUED folder is polled; the folder ID is pinned, not name-matched
filename text never grants authority; authority is folder membership by pinned ID
writes outside approved folders fail closed
mutation denied without an activated mutation TaskEnvelope
the exactly-once key binds command ID, Drive ID, and Drive revision
an unresolved claim prevents a second claim
monotonic fencing enforced; a zombie with an unexpired lease but a superseded token is refused
the spool is append-only and collision-safe via exclusive create
a Drive outage drops nothing and overwrites nothing; spool precedes the network call
secret values are redacted while keys remain readable
protected workbooks and source evidence cannot be uploaded, by digest, suffix, mime type, and ZIP signature
the HOLD cannot be removed or altered by any code path
canonical Drive URLs are rebuilt from verified IDs; metadata viewUrl is never reused
no non-Google URL is followed or trusted; docichat.com and livepolls.app are explicitly denied

secret_scan_incident.summary: Committing the build tripped the repository secret scanner three times before going green. All values involved were fabricated test fixtures; no real credential was ever committed or exposed.
secret_scan_incident.root_cause_1: redaction fixtures written as literals, including a generic-api-key match on an api_key=<value> pair
secret_scan_incident.root_cause_2: the gitleaks allowlist form differs by version; the pinned CI image requires the plural [[allowlists]] table and errors out if a singular [allowlist] table is also present
secret_scan_incident.latent_defect_found: the repository's pre-existing ad02fdeb allowlist entry sits in a form that older local gitleaks builds ignore, so a local reproduction over-reports relative to CI
secret_scan_incident.resolution: all fixtures are built at runtime, parametrise with explicit ids so values never reach caches or CI logs, and the config uses the plural form only
secret_scan_incident.process_note: The first two diagnoses were reasoned from rule definitions rather than reproduced, and both were wrong. The fix was only correct once a local gitleaks binary reproduced both CI steps.

next_permitted_action: Copy the repository to the authorized Windows workstation, run run_control_tower.bat selftest and confirm 18/18, then run run_control_tower.bat audit with DBX_V12_PATH set to the pinned V12 path. Only if that audit returns exit 0 with v12_ruling VERIFIED_EXACT may Gate 0 be claimed, and claiming remains a separate deliberate step requiring owner direction.
